newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Salomon sees high Chinese airline growth prospects.
newsitem.headline: Salomon sees high Chinese airline growth prospects.

text.p: The Chinese airline industry's long term growth prospects are among the best in the world and traffic is forecast to grow at 15 to 20 percent annually over the coming years, Salomon Brothers said in a report.
It added that Chinese airlines have arguably the highest growth potential of any national airline industry in the world.
Buoyed by a strong economy growing at around 10 percent per year, the traffic growth forecasts should easily be underpinned, but it did not define the exact period covered.

Tourism and travel will mushroom, helped by key structural changes, improving ties with the U.S. and recent codeshare agreements with U.S. carriers. By facilitating business travel of either China nationals or foreigners, the airline industry becomes a principal contributor to promoting investment, it said.
The Chinese government acting through the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) is expected to force a partial rationalisation of the fragmented airline industry, the report added.

Consolidation will give the three major airlines - China Eastern Airlines Corp Ltd, Air China and China Southern - exciting growth prospects. But the report warned growth would be determined by external assessments of safety and security, it said.
Chinese airlines also have a bigger task ahead of them than other Asian carriers facing the problem of managing growth and keeping costs under control, the report added.

"As with any fledgling international business, the Chinese majors must undertake substantial development and improve the overall sophistication of their product. One of the likely short term incentives is that all three major airlines have reasonably young fleets, which means they are employing expensive aircraft across their networks."
"As the airline industry traditionally has a high fixed cost basis, the Chinese carriers should eventually become as revenue focused as their western counterparts," the report said.
However, Chinese airline managements are also burdened by a funding shortfall which threatens to limit the realisation of their potential. it added.

The country also needs to invest heavily in infrastructure to overcome distribution problems which are the greatest limiting factor to economic prosperity,it said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
